data.title: Choose the sentence that uses the word correctly.

sections.question: application
sections.summary: A formal written request for a job, place on a course or other opportunity; also used to mean a computer program or the practical use of a skill.

senses.definition: a formal written or online request for a job, place on a course or other opportunity
examples: She submitted her application for the marketing position two days before the closing date.

senses.definition: the practical use of a theory, skill or rule in a real situation
examples: The application of new technology has transformed the way the company manages its data.

answers.answer: She sent her application to five different companies and received two interview invitations.
He wore his best application to the job interview at the company's head office.
She used her application to pay for lunch at the office canteen every day of the week.
The application was very comfortable and had an excellent view of the city skyline.

sections.question: benefits
sections.summary: Additional advantages provided by an employer beyond a basic salary, such as health insurance, a pension or paid leave; also general advantages or positive effects.

senses.definition: extra advantages offered by an employer in addition to salary, such as health insurance, a company car or paid holidays
examples: The position comes with excellent benefits, including private healthcare and a company pension.

senses.definition: money paid by the government to people who are unemployed, ill or in need of support
examples: He claimed unemployment benefits for three months while he was looking for a new job.

answers.answer: The job offers a competitive salary as well as excellent benefits including flexible working hours.
She showed great benefits in completing the project well ahead of the expected schedule.
He ate the benefits quickly and returned to his desk before the lunch break was over.
The benefits were so heavy that it took two assistants to carry them to the conference room.

sections.question: contract
sections.summary: A formal legal agreement between two or more parties, setting out terms and conditions; also used as a verb meaning to make a legal agreement or to become smaller.

senses.definition: a written legal agreement between two or more people or organisations
examples: She signed a two-year contract with the company after completing her three-month probation period.

senses.definition: to make a formal legal agreement to do something
examples: The company contracted an external firm to handle all of its marketing activities.

senses.definition: to become smaller or shorter; or to catch an illness
examples: Metals contract when the temperature drops significantly.

answers.answer: He read the contract carefully and asked a lawyer to check the terms before signing it.
She showed great contract in negotiating her salary and secured a much higher starting offer.
He contract to arrive at the office by nine o'clock every morning without fail.
The contract was very comfortable and had a pleasant view of the company garden from the window.

sections.question: entrepreneur
sections.summary: A person who starts and runs their own business, often taking on financial risks in the hope of making a profit.

senses.definition: someone who starts their own business, especially when this involves taking financial risks
examples: The young entrepreneur launched her first online business from her bedroom at the age of nineteen.

answers.answer: The entrepreneur secured funding from investors and opened her second restaurant within a year.
He was a very entrepreneur employee who always arrived early and never missed a deadline.
She showed great entrepreneur in completing all her tasks efficiently before the end of the week.
The entrepreneur was very tasty and all the guests thoroughly enjoyed it at the conference dinner.

sections.question: internship
sections.summary: A temporary position, often unpaid or low-paid, in which a student or recent graduate gains practical work experience in a professional environment.

senses.definition: a short period of work experience, often unpaid, undertaken by a student or recent graduate to gain skills in a particular field
examples: She completed a six-month internship at a law firm before graduating from university.

answers.answer: The internship gave him valuable experience in the finance industry and led directly to a job offer.
She showed great internship in solving the complex problem that her line manager had presented.
He put his internship in his bag and showed it to the interviewer at the start of the meeting.
The internship was very comfortable and had excellent facilities for the permanent members of staff.

sections.question: job description
sections.summary: A written document that explains the duties, responsibilities and requirements of a particular job or position.

senses.definition: a formal document outlining the responsibilities, duties and requirements of a specific job or position
examples: She read the job description carefully before deciding whether to apply for the position.

answers.answer: The job description listed strong communication skills and five years of experience as essential requirements.
He showed great job description in explaining his role clearly to the new members of the team.
She wore the job description to the interview and made an excellent first impression on the panel.
The job description was very comfortable and offered an excellent view of the park from the window.

sections.question: negotiation
sections.summary: A formal discussion between two or more parties aimed at reaching an agreement; also the process of navigating through or past something.

senses.definition: a formal discussion between people or groups who are trying to reach an agreement
examples: After a week of intensive negotiation, the two companies finally agreed on the terms of the contract.

answers.answer: Skilled negotiation helped her secure a salary that was fifteen percent higher than the initial offer.
She felt great negotiation when the company finally accepted her request for a pay rise.
He packed his negotiation into his briefcase before heading to the important client meeting.
The negotiation was very comfortable and had a beautiful view of the river from the meeting room.

sections.question: profession
sections.summary: A type of paid work that requires a high level of education or specialist training; also all the people who work in a particular field.

senses.definition: a type of job that requires advanced education or specialist training, such as medicine, law or teaching
examples: Teaching is a demanding profession that requires both academic knowledge and strong people skills.

senses.definition: all the people who work in a particular profession as a group
examples: The medical profession has called for greater investment in mental health services.

answers.answer: She chose nursing as her profession because she wanted to make a real difference to people's lives.
She showed great profession throughout the project, always communicating clearly and meeting every deadline.
He wore his best profession to the annual company awards ceremony at the end of the year.
The profession was very comfortable and had an excellent view from the corner office window.

sections.question: recruitment
sections.summary: The process of finding and hiring new people to work for a company or organisation.

senses.definition: the process of finding, selecting and hiring people for jobs or positions within an organisation
examples: The company launched a major recruitment drive to hire fifty new engineers by the end of the year.

answers.answer: The human resources team is responsible for all recruitment within the organisation.
She attended the recruitment every morning to improve her fitness before the summer holidays.
He put the recruitment in his briefcase and brought it to the early morning meeting with the director.
The recruitment was very comfortable and offered a beautiful view of the park from the window.

sections.question: resignation
sections.summary: The act of formally leaving a job or position; also a feeling of calm acceptance of something difficult or unavoidable.

senses.definition: the act of formally giving up a job or position
examples: She handed in her resignation after being offered a senior position at a competing firm.

senses.definition: calm acceptance of something difficult or unpleasant that cannot be changed
examples: He accepted the news of the restructure with resignation and began to update his CV.

answers.answer: The manager's sudden resignation came as a surprise to the rest of the team.
She put on her resignation and walked confidently into the boardroom for the final presentation.
He felt great resignation when his team won the quarterly sales competition for the third time.
The resignation was very comfortable and had a pleasant view of the company car park below.
